name: VyReel
summary: Shopify app that turns Instagram and TikTok reels or your own UGC into shoppable carousels, stories, grids and a watch-and-buy viewer, with AI product tagging on every plan.
best_for: Shopify stores that already publish short-form video on Instagram or TikTok and want it on the storefront as shoppable reels, stories and grids, with AI product tagging included from the free tier up
skip_if: you sell outside Shopify; you have no video to feed it, since the app displays and tags clips rather than making them; or you run high traffic and need to know your cost at the click cap before committing, which neither pricing page tells you
honest_knock:
The meter is clicks, and nobody says what happens when you run out. Every tier is sized on storefront clicks a month (500 free, 10,000 on Basic, 30,000 on Growth, 75,000 on Pro) alongside a cap on uploaded videos. Neither the Shopify listing nor the vendor's own pricing section says whether the reels stop, degrade or trigger a charge when a busy month crosses the line, and no overage rate is published. The better your videos work, the faster you use the allowance, so ask support what happens at the cap before a sale weekend answers the question for you.

The track record is three months long. The app launched on the Shopify App Store on 19 June 2026, and its eight reviews (counted 11 November 2026), all five stars, were written between 20 June and 23 July 2026, each after anything from about an hour to 21 days of use. Two of them, both dated 23 July, come from stores listed as "Maryum & Maria" and "Maryum N Maria". Five of the eight reviewing stores are in Pakistan. A 5.0 from eight early reviews tells you the setup is quick; it does not tell you how the app behaves at 50,000 clicks a month or after a year of theme updates.

The two pricing pages do not match. The listing stops at Pro, $79 a month; the vendor's own site adds Scale at $129 and Enterprise at $199, and reserves its advanced AI tagging for those two. The attribution panel on the vendor's homepage ($48,210 attributed revenue, 3.1x ROAS on video) names no customer and reads as an illustration, not a reported result.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Basic · per month for 10,000 storefront clicks and 50 videos, billed through Shopify every 30 days with a 14-day free trial
pricing.notes: (read 2026-09-24 on apps.shopify.com/vyreel and on the vendor's own pricing section at vy-reel.com; re-read unchanged on 2026-11-11) The Shopify listing shows four tiers, the vendor site six. Free: 500 storefront clicks a month and up to 5 video uploads, with every feature and AI product tagging included; the vendor site labels it Trial, $0 forever. Basic is $19 a month, or $182 a year, for 10,000 clicks and 50 videos. Growth is $49 a month, or $470 a year, for 30,000 clicks and 150 videos with priority email support. Pro is $79 a month, or $758 a year, for 75,000 clicks and 300 videos with priority email support. Two more tiers appear only on vy-reel.com: Scale at $129 a month for 150,000 clicks, 500 videos, advanced AI product tagging and priority in-app chat, and Enterprise at $199 a month for unlimited clicks and videos with dedicated support. Every paid tier starts with a 14-day free trial. Annual billing saves 20%; the listing quotes it as a yearly figure, while the vendor's own billing note says annual plans are charged as monthly payments at the discount rather than as one upfront charge. All charges are in USD through Shopify's billing, every 30 days.

compare_with.name: Storista
compare_with.why: Storista is the closest comparison in our own dossiers, and it meters the other way round. Storista (read 23 August 2026) counts videos and leaves views unlimited: 10 videos free, 50 for $15 a month, unlimited for $49, with its AI Smart Tagging only from that $49 tier. VyReel counts storefront clicks and videos together: 5 videos and 500 clicks free, 50 videos and 10,000 clicks for $19, and AI product tagging on every tier including the free one. So a store that wants automatic tagging on a small library pays less here, while a store with heavy traffic on a modest library is safer on Storista, whose views are never metered. Storista also carries Shopify's Built for Shopify badge and has been listed since 2021; VyReel's listing, launched in June 2026, carries no badge yet.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested the start of VyReel on a Shopify development store: the install from the app address in the admin, because the Install button in the App Store did not work for our test tool, the Free trial with 0 of 5 videos and 0 of 500 clicks, the Product Library with 23 products that need a reel, the Billing page with six plans, the Shopify approval screen for Basic (a 14-day trial; it said there would be no test charge but also asked for a payment method; nothing approved) and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. The core action, uploading a video and showing it in a widget, could not be tested: the upload page sits in an iframe from another domain that our test tool cannot operate. That is a limit of our test and not a fault of the app. Nothing was paid. Install: the Install button on the App Store listing (apps.shopify.com/vyreel, English) did not work for our test tool: in our own tab it led back to the listing twice without an install and once opened an extra tab outside our tab group (that tab could not be closed by us). The install started at 20:56 and succeeded at about 20:57 by opening the app address in the Shopify admin (the apps page of the app), pressing Install app and then Install in the dialog, which said the app needs access to View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data. No plan screen and no payment screen came with the install and the app started on the Free trial plan. The app then showed an onboarding Let's get your reels live (5 steps: Upload, Tag & show, Collection, App embed, Go live) with no terms tick box; Skip onboarding was clicked. No vendor account, password, Google login, call or phone number was asked. Core action NOT tested: the plan was to upload a short test clip, tag a product and show it in a widget in the preview. The upload page (0 of 5 videos on the Free trial plan; MP4, MOV or WebM up to 1 GB each) sits in an iframe from another domain. Our test tool could not see or use anything inside that iframe: it found no file field, clicking Choose files opens a native file dialog that the tool cannot operate, and opening the iframe address directly led back to the Shopify admin. So no video was uploaded, nothing was tagged and no widget was seen. This is a limit of our test tool and not a fault of the app; whether the upload works was NOT tested. Instagram and TikTok were deliberately not connected. Without a video we only saw the Product Library, which showed Needs a reel 23 and Has a reel 0 with a button + Attach a reel for each product; no sample video or demo option was found. Until the upload block it took about 4 steps (install dialog, Install, skip onboarding) and about 3 minutes; the time to a first result was not reached. Plans in the app (Billing page, Monthly; an Annual switch says save 20%): the page opened on CURRENT PLAN Free trial (Active since 2026-11-17), VIDEOS 0 / 5 total, STOREFRONT CLICKS 0 / 500 (resets 2026-12-17) and AT THE CLICK CAP Carousel hides. Six plans are shown: Free trial, Free, 500 storefront clicks a month, 5 videos total; Basic $19 a month, 10,000 clicks, 50 videos; Growth $49 a month, 30,000 clicks, 150 videos, Priority email support; Pro $79 a month (MOST POPULAR), 75,000 clicks, 300 videos, Priority email support; Scale $129 a month, 150,000 clicks, 500 videos, Advanced AI product tagging, Priority in-app chat support; Enterprise $199 a month (PREMIUM), Unlimited clicks, Unlimited videos, Advanced AI product tagging, Highest processing concurrency, Priority in-app chat plus dedicated support. The App Store listing shows four plans, so Scale and Enterprise are only in the app. At the click cap the app says Carousel hides; what really happens at the cap was not tested and no overage price is shown anywhere. Checkout: Choose Basic opened the Shopify screen Approve subscription: a yellow bar You will not be billed for this test charge., the plan VyReel Basic (monthly), $19,00 USD every 30 days, You have a 14-day free trial ending on 1 Dec., Subtotal $19,00 plus any applicable taxes, Total $19,00 Due 1 Dec, and also a row Add payment method (no stored payment method was shown). Because a payment method seemed to be needed and no card may be entered, the charge was not approved; Cancel was clicked and the app showed Charge declined. No money was paid and no subscription started. Cancelling: no subscription ran. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, the menu of the app and Uninstall: the dialog Uninstall VyReel? says that you can no longer use the app, that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information; a reason had to be chosen (Testing multiple apps) before the uninstall. Not tested: the video upload (blocked by our test tool, see above), product tagging and AI tagging, the widget in the theme editor or preview, the carousel, stories and grid, Analytics, the Instagram and TikTok import, Collections, Settings, what happens at the click cap and the Free trial limits in use. Clean up: the app was uninstalled at about 21:03 and no longer shows under installed apps. No product, no theme change and no upload was made and no card was entered. Our own tab was closed; the extra tab that the App Store button opened is outside our tab group and may still be open in our browser. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The Install button on the App Store listing did not install the app for our test tool and one click opened an extra tab outside our tab group; the app address in the admin worked. The Billing page names a click cap ("Carousel hides") but shows no overage price, and the approval screen said there would be no test charge but still asked for a payment method.
